la:verb:prosum.gloss: to be useful or of use, do good, help, benefit, profit
senses: to be useful or of use, do good, help, benefit, profit
la:verb:prosum.html:
prō-sum, fŭi, prōdesse, v. n.,
to be useful or of use, to do good, benefit, profit.
In gen., constr. with dat., a subjectclause, or absol., rarely with ad or in and acc.: sibi prodesse, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 310 Vahl.); cf.: qui nec sibi nec alteri prosunt,: multis,: nihil tibi litterae meae proderunt,.—With subj.-clause: multum prodest ea quae metuuntur ipsa contemnere,: iis carum et jucundum esse maxime prodest,; cf. : quid mihi fingere prodest?: nec quicquam tibi prodest Aërias tentasse domos,; ; : quae scire magis juvat quam prodest,.—Absol.: prodesse aequom est,: quorum altera prosunt, Cin. Fin. 3, 21, 69: studia aliena ac nihil profutura,: magis tamen Menenianum profuit judicium,; ; : quae nocuere sequar, fugiam quae profore credam,: aut prodesse volunt aut delectare poëtae,: tu tantum corpore prodes, Nos animo,.— With ad or in and acc.: id mirum, quantum profuit ad concordiam civitatis,: in id quoque prodest, ut, etc.,: in commune,.—With abl.: constantia multum prodest in amore,.—
In partic., of medicines, to be good, be beneficial: fabam voci prodesse,: balineum assumo, quia prodest,: ad tormina,: contra ignem sacrum,.—With inf.: contra anginas tritum in poscā gargarizare prodest,.

la:verb:prospecto.gloss: to look or gaze out at; to behold
senses: to look or gaze out at; to behold
la:verb:prospecto.html:
prospecto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a.
prospicio
,
to look forth upon, look out; to look at, view, behold, see afar off, gaze upon: mare,.
Lit.: pars ex tectis fenestrisque prospectant,; cf. : Campani moenia urbis prospectantes repleverant,: hostem,: e terrā aliquem,: intenti proelium equestre prospectabant,: incendium e turri,: e puppi pontum,: Capitolia ab excelsā aede,: prospectans maesta carinam,.—Absol.: astris prospectantibus,.—Impers. pass.: quā longissime prospectari poterat,.—
Transf.
To look around or about: prospectare, ne uspiam insidiae sient,.—
Of localities, to look towards, to lie or be situate towards any quarter (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): villa, quae monte summo posita Prospectat Siculum,: villa, quae subjectos sinus editissima prospectat,: septentrionem,: locus late prospectans,furnishing a wide prospect,: thermae prospicientes viam sacram, (9), 27, 18: hos (campos) ad occasum conversa prospectat,; ; .—
Trop.
To look forward to, to expect a thing; to hope, look out for, await (class.): exsilium,: diem de die prospectans, ecquod auxilium ab dictatore appareret,.—
To await, impend over, threaten one: te quoque fata Prospectant paria,.—
To foresee (post-class.): prospectandi cognitio,.

la:verb:proscripturio.html:
prōscriptŭrĭo, īre,
v. desider. n [id], to desire or long to proscribe, (a word formed

sarcastically by Cic.): ita sullaturit animus ejus et proscripturit diu, (cited ).

la:verb:prospicio.gloss: to look far off; to see into the distance
senses: to look far off; to see into the distance
to watch or look out for
to foresee, see ahead, look forward or towards something
la:verb:prospicio.html:
prō-spĭcĭo, exi, ectum, 3, v. n. and a.
[specio].
Neutr., to look forward or into the distance, to look out, to look, see (class.).
In gen.: neque post respiciens, neque ante prospiciens, Varr. ap. : parum prospiciunt oculi,do not see well,; : grues volant ad prospiciendum alte,: ex superioribus locis prospicere in urbem,: multum,to have an extensive prospect,: per umbram,: procul,: ex moenibus,: longe lateque, Auct. B. Hisp. 8.—
In partic.
To look out, to watch, be on the watch: puer ab januā prospiciens,: pavorem simulans (feles) prospexit toto die,: Michol prospiciens per fenestram,; cf. .—
To look or see to beforehand, to exercise foresight, to look out for, take care of, provide for any thing: ego jam prospiciam mihi,: consulere ac prospicere debemus, ut, etc.,: prospicite atque consulite,, § 22: ut prospicias et consulas rationibus meis,: consulite vobis, prospicite patriae,: homo longe in posterum prospiciens,: ut illum intellegatis non longe animo prospexisse morientem,: prospicite, ut, etc.,: statuebat prospiciendum, ne, etc.,: in annum,.—Impers. pass.: senatusconsulto prospectum est, ne, etc.,.— Absol.: malo nos prospicere quam ulcisci,

: plagae crescunt, Nisi prospicis,.—

Act., to see afar off, to discern, descry, espy.
In gen. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): Italiam summā ab undā,: campos Prospexit longe,; : moenia urbis Tarpeiā de rupe,: ex speculis adventantem hostium classem,: ut hostium agmen inde prospicerent,: ex edito monte cuncta,.—
Transf., of situations, to have or command a view of, look or lie towards, to overlook: domus prospicit agros,: cenatio latissimum mare, amoenissimas villas prospicit,; ; : freta prospiciens Tmolus,; .—
Trop.: aliquis infans decessit, cui nihil amplius contigit quam prospicere vitam,to see life from a distance, to get a glimpse of,: turpe est seni aut prospicienti senectutem, etc.,one who sees old age before him,: neque prospexisse castra,i. e. life in camp,.—
In partic.
To look at attentively, to gaze at (very rare): aliquem propter aliquid,.—
To foresee a thing (class.): multo ante, tamquam ex aliquā speculā, prospexi tempestatem futuram,; cf.: longe prospicere futuros casus rei publicae,; : multum in posterum,: ex imbri soles,. —With rel.-clause: ut jam ante animo prospicere possis, quibus de rebus auditurus sis,; .—
To look out for, provide, procure: habitationem alicui,: sedem senectuti,: maritum filiae,.—In pass.: nisi si prospectum interea aliquid est, desertae vivimus,: commeatus a praetore prospectos in hiemem habere,: ad ferramenta prospicienda,.—Hence,
prōspĭcĭ-ens, entis, P. a., endowed with foresight, .—
prōspĭcĭenter, adv., providently, considerately, carefully (post-class.): res prospicienter animadversas,.—
prōspectē, adv., providently, deliberately, considerately, advisedly, prudently (post-class.): decernere,.—Sup.: adhaerebit bono,.
la:verb:prospicio.inflection: exi, ectum, 3, v. n. and a.

la:noun:prospectus.html:
prospectus, ūs, m.
prospicio
.
Lit., a lookout, distant view, prospect (class.): sterilis prospectus,: cum saepibus prospectus impediretur,; cf. : non prospectu modo extra vallum adempto, sed propinquo etiam congredientium inter se conspectu,: petere prospectum ex arce,: habere prospectum in praeceps,.—
Transf.
Sight, view: aliquem in prospectum populi Romani producere,: cum jam extremi essent in prospectu,to be in sight,; cf. : lugubris,: praeclarus,: praebere prospectum navium,: prospectum eripiens oculis,.—
Poet., sight, vision: late Aequora prospectu metior,.—
Trop.
Regard, respect (post-class.): cujus rationem prospectumque Bias non habuit,; so, prospectum officii deponere,ext.—
Foresight (eccl. Lat.): humanus prospectus,.

senses: to attend, wait on, allow, accommodate
la:verb:prosequor.html:
prō-sĕquor, cūtus (quūtus), 3,
v. dep. a., to follow (in a friendly or hostile manner), to accompany, attend; to follow after, pursue (class.; cf.: comitor, stipo).
Lit.: novum maritum volo rus prosequi,: eum milites electi circiter CXX. sunt prosecuti,: Dianam ture odoribusque incensis prosecutae sunt,; : unum omnes illum prosequebantur,: aliquem in domum,: exsequias,to attend a funeral,; so, defunctum in conditorium,; cf.: Bassus noster videtur mihi prosequi se,to attend his own funeral,: lacrimis ad saevas prosequor usque fores,; : Aeneas Prosequitur lacrimans longe,; .—In a hostile sense, to follow after, pursue: fugientes prosequi,: hostem,: novissimos multa millia passuum prosecuti,; : iste iratus hominem verbis vehementioribus prosequitur,i. e. assailed, attacked,: aliquem contumeliosis vocibus,: speculatores, qui prosequerentur agmen, missi,; : armati qui eos prosequebantur,: aliquem lapidibus,.—Of animals: eādem cane anxie prosequente,; .—With abl., of following with the eyes: oculis abeuntem prosequor udis,; : aliquos visu,.—
Transf., of inanim. and abstr. subjects, to follow, pursue; to accompany, attend: prosequitur surgens a puppi ventus euntes,: naves mitterent quae se prosequerentur,; cf. exercitus,; : datae duae triremes ad prosequendum,: Cattos suos saltus Hercynius prosequitur simul atque deponit,goes as far as their territory extends, and then ceases,: eadem (existimatio Quintum) usque ad rogum prosequatur,; cf.: (amici) mortui vivunt: tantus eos honos prosequitur amicorum,.—
Trop.
To honor, adorn, or present one with a thing, to bestow any thing upon one; constr. with abl., rarely with cum and abl.: benevolentiā, aut misericordiā prosequi aliquem,: aliquem honorificis verbis,: virtutem alicujus gratā memoriā,: nomen alicujus grato animo,: memoriam cujuspiam clamore et plausu,: aliquem laudibus,: aliquem beneficiis ac liberalitate,: cum me in illo tristi et acerbo luctu atque discessu non lacrimis solum tuis, sed animo, corpore, copiis prosecutus esses,; cf.: reliquum est ut tuam profectionem amore prosequar, reditum spe exspectem,: delictum veniā,: Maximum libenter apud te testimonio prosequar, (17): prosecuti cum donis legatos sunt,: decedentem domum cum favore ac laudibus prosecuti sunt,: Senatus gratias egit Caesari, quod et ipse cum summo honore mentionem ejus prosecutus esset,; cf.: aliquem uberrimo congiario,: milites,.—
To pursue, continue, follow up, to go on or proceed with an idea or theme: si (rem) non ad extremum, sed usque eo, quo opus erit, prosequemur,: non prosequar longius,: illius vero mortis opportunitatem benevolentiā prosequamur,: pascua versu,to describe at length,: stilo munificentiae rationem,: ut latius, quae cujusque adfectus natura sit, prosequamur,; : uno libello carissimam mihi memoriam prosequi, : ex ordine domesticos motus, to pursue, go through with, describe in order, Flor 3, 12, 14: similitudinem,to follow up,.—Absol., to proceed with one's speaking (poet.): prosequitur pavitans, et ficto pectore fatur,.

senses: alternative form of prosperus (singular masculine nominative)
la:adj:prosper.html:
prosper, and more freq. prospĕrus, a. um, adj.
pro-spero, answering to hope; cf. spes
,
agreeable to one's wishes, favorable, fortunate, prosperous (freq. and class.; cf.: faustus, propitius): sperem veteres pro spem dixerunt, unde et prospere dicimus, hoc est, pro spe,: auspicium prosperum,; cf. in sup.: prosperrimum augurium,: prospera adversaque fortuna,: magnis autem viris prosperae semper omnes res,: prosperae res,: non jam id ago, ut prosperos exitus consequar,: successus, Liv. praef. fin.: prosperrimo rerum eventu,.—Comp.: prosperior civium amor,: mox cecinit laudes prosperiore lyrā,: prosperius fatum,: nomina,of good omen,; so, verba,.—In nom. sing.: prosper dicendi successus, Auct. ap. P.; : deinde est hominum generi prosperus et salutaris ille fulgor, qui dicitur Jovis,propitious, favorable, (cited in P.): immoriens magnis non prosperus ausis,: prosperus in Africam transitus,.—With evenio (cf. prospere): omnia quae prospera tibi evenere,: si cetera prospera evenissent,: quod bellum ... ut id prosperum eveniret,; .—
With gen. (poet.): noctilucam. Prosperam frugum,beneficial to fruits,.—
Subst., in plur.: prospĕra, ōrum, n., favorable circumstances, good fortune, prosperity (postAug.): prospera belli,: rerum,: tam mala Pompeii quam prospera mundus adoret,: Germani prosperis feroces,; .—Hence, adv., in two forms.
pro-spĕrē, agreeably to one's wishes, favorably, luckily, fortunately, prosperously (class.): omnia profluenter, prospere,: procedere,: cedere alicui,: succedere,: cui ut omnia prospere evenirent,: cadere,.— Comp.: aves quae prosperius evolant,with better augury,: res eventura prosperius,; .—Sup.: prosperrĭme geruntur omnia. : dimicare,.—*
prospĕ-rĭter, favorably, fortunately, Enn. ap. P.

la:verb:prospero.html:
prospĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
prosper
.
To cause a thing to succeed, to render fortunate or happy, to prosper (syn. secundo; not in Cic.): vos precor, uti populo Romano Quiritium vim victoriamque prosperetis, an old form of prayer in : ut consilia sua reipublicae prosperarent,: deos precatus, ut coepta prosperarent,; cf.: patrum decreta,: hanc tibi veniam prospero, i. e. make you happy with, etc., : prosperata felicitas,desired happiness,: mala averruncare, bona prosperare,.—Absol.: amico meo prosperabo,will make my friend happy,: non prosperantibus avibus,the birds not giving favorable omens,.—With inf.: qui prosperavit mundari locum,.—Pass.: via impiorum prosperatur,.—
To render favorable or propitious, to propitiate (post-class.): prosperatus deus, Prud. στεφ. 10, 365: o Domine, bene prosperare, (118), 25.

la:verb:proscribo.html:
prō-scrībo, psi, ptum, 3, v. a.,
to write before or in front of, to write over or upon, to inscribe.
In gen. (post-Aug.): vultus voluntariā poenarum lege proscripti,written over, inscribed,.—
In partic.
To publish any thing by writing (freq. and class.): ut quo die esse oporteret idus Januarias, eo die Calendas Martias proscriberet,: quam (legem) non is promulgavit, quo nomine proscriptam videtis,, § 177: non proscriptā neque edictā die,: venationem,: leges,: versiculos per vias,.—
With obj.-clause: senatum Calendis velle se frequentem adesse, etiam Formiis proscribi jussit,: proscribit se auctionem esse facturum,; cf. .—
To offer in writing any thing for sale, lease, or hire, or as to be sold by auction, to post up, advertise: proscribere palam sic accipimus, claris litteris, ut, etc.,: Racilius tabulam proscripsit, se familiam Catonianam venditurum,: Claudius proscripsit insulam, vendidit,.—
To publish a person as having forfeited his property, to punish with confiscation, to confiscate one's property (cf. publico): quaero enim, quid sit aliud proscribere. Velitis, jubeatis, ut M. Tullius in civitate ne sit, bonaque ejus ut mea sint,: Pompeium,to confiscate the estates gained by him,: vicinos,to confiscate the lands of one's neighbors,: possessiones,: bona,.—
To proscribe, outlaw one, by hanging up a tablet with his name and sentence of outlawry, confiscation of goods, etc.: posteaquam victoria constituta est, cum proscriberentur homines, qui adversarii fuisse putabantur,: victoriā Sullae parentes,: modus proscribendi,.—Hence, P. a., as subst.: prōscriptus, i, an outlaw, one proscribed: contra legem Corneliam, quae proscriptum juvari vetat,: proscriptorum liberos honores petere puduit,: in proscriptorum numero esse,: bona proscriptorum, Dietsch.—
Trop.: cujus pudoris dignitas in concione proscripta sit,has been brought into ill repute, rendered suspected,.

la:other:Proserpina.gloss: Proserpina or Proserpine, daughter of Ceres and Jupiter; wife of Pluto, who seized her as she was gathering flowers in Sicily, and carried her to Hades to be queen of the Underworld; equivalent to Greek Persephone, goddess of the seasons and spring vegetation; conflated with earlier Italic Roman deity Libera
senses: Proserpina or Proserpine, daughter of Ceres and Jupiter; wife of Pluto, who seized her as she was gathering flowers in Sicily, and carried her to Hades to be queen of the Underworld; equivalent to Greek Persephone, goddess of the seasons and spring vegetation; conflated with earlier Italic Roman deity Libera
la:other:Proserpina.html:
Prō^serpĭna, ae, f., = Περσεφόνη.
Proserpine, daughter of Ceres and Jupiter, and wife of Pluto, who seized her as she was gathering flowers in Sicily, and carried her away to the infernal regions: Cereris Proserpina puer,; cf. ; ; ; .—
Poet., for the Lower World: sed me Imperiosa trahit Proserpina: vive, valeque,.

la:verb:prosilio.gloss: to leap, jump, rush or spring forth or up
senses: to leap, jump, rush or spring forth or up
to burst or break forth, start out, start up
to leap to or attempt eagerly
la:verb:prosilio.html:
prō-sĭlĭo, ŭi (less freq. īvi or ĭi;
īvi,; ; ; ii,; ), 4 (fut. prosilibo for prosiliam, Auct. ), v. n.
salio
, to leap or spring forth, to spring up (class.).
Lit.: quidnam hic properans prosilit,: repente prosiluerunt,: ex tabernaculo,: ab sede,: puppe,: stratis,: de capitis paterni Vertice (of Minerva),: e convivio,: de navi,: in contionem,: in proelium,: ad accusationem,: ad flumen,: in publicum,: donec prosilit unus,.—
Transf., of inanim. subjects, to spring or burst forth, to start out (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): (sanguis) Emicat, et longe terebrata prosilit aura,: prosiliunt lacrimae,: prosilit scintilla,: castanea sponte prosiliens,: frutices in altitudinem prosiliunt,shoot up, grow,: Peloponnesi prosilit cervix,i. e. the isthmus begins and runs out,.—
Trop.
To break forth (poet.): vaga prosiliet frenis natura remotis,.—
To

start up, to hasten (poet.): prosilui amicum castigatum,.—

To leap to any thing, attempt zealously or eagerly (mostly poet.): numquam nisi potus ad arma Prosiluit dicenda,: ad certamen,: ad accusationem,; : ad munus, Cod. 10, 52, 7.

la:verb:prosequere.gloss: second-person singular present active imperative/indicative of prōsequor
senses: second-person singular present active imperative/indicative of prōsequor
to prostrate, knock down, throw to the ground
la:verb:prosterno.html:
prō-sterno, strāvi, strātum, 3, v. a.,
to strew in front of, to strew before one; also, to throw to the ground, throw down, overthrow, prostrate (syn.: fundo, profligo, provolvo).
Lit.: eo prosternebant folia farferi, (al. praesternebant): ceteros ruerem ... et prosternerem,: pondere silvam,: prostraturus humi corpus,; cf. : se ad pedes alicujus,; so, prosternere se et supplicare alicui,: his auditis prostraverant se omnes humi,: hostem prostravit, fudit, occidit,: hostem ferro,: legio prosternitur latis arvis,: telo virum,: lapsu equi prostratus,.—
Trop.
To throw to the ground, to overthrow, subvert, ruin, destroy, etc. (freq. and class.): omnia cupiditate ac furore,; ; cf.: jacet ille nunc prostratus,; and: afflicta ct prostrata virtus,; : malevolorum obtrectationes, Vatin. ap. : mores civitatis,: carminum studium,: se prosternere, to demean or debase one's self, : prostrata est Philisthaea omnis,.—
To prostitute, ; ; ; ; (in Plin Pan. 31 the true read. is praesterni).

la:noun:prosperitas.html:
prospĕrĭtas, ātis, f.
prosper
,
desirable condition, good fortune, success, prosperity (rare but good prose): vitae,: honestarum rerum, id. Fragm. ap. : tantā prosperitate usus est valetudinis, ut, etc.,such a desirable state of health, such full health,.—In plur.: improborum prosperitates secundaeque res,: ventorum,: summarum rerum,: currentes ex voto,; .—
Joy, approbation: quod est prosperitatis indicium plenum,.

senses: to creep along, to crawl along
la:verb:proserpo.html:
prō-serpo, ĕre, v. n.,
to creep forwards or forth, to creep or crawl along (ante- and post-class.).
Lit.: proserpens bestia,; cf. ; ; Müll.: servulus proserpit leniter,: de specu funesta proserpit ursa,, p. 198, 25.—Transf., of plants, to come forth imperceptibly: sata in lucem proserpunt,.—
Trop., to move on imperceptibly, to glide or steal along (postclass.): proserpit ad intima vulnus,: malo proserpenti occurrere,.

la:noun:proscriptio.html:
prōscriptĭo, ōnis, f.
proscribo
(class.).
A written public notice of sale. an advertisement: proscriptio bonorum,: quam ad diem proscriptiones venditionesque fiant,: bonorum,: praediorum,.—
Proscription, outlawry, confiscation: proscriptionis miserrimum nomen,: de capite civis et de bonis proscriptionem ferre,; : capitis mei,: proscriptione pecunias ex aerario accipere,.

la:verb:prostituo.html:
prō-stĭtŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. a.
statuo
.
To place before or in front, . —
To expose publicly to prostitution, to prostitute: cras populo prostituam vos,; : quae (meretrix) sese toto corpore prostituit,: pudicitiam suam,; : formam,: faciem suam lucro,: corpora libidinibus,; : virgines,.—
Transf.: famam alicujus, to prostitute, dishonor, sully, Cato ap. : ingrato vocem foro,.—Hence, prōstĭtūtus, a, um, P. a., exposed publicly, prostituted: infans, P.—Sup.: prostitutissima lupa Larentina,.—Subst.: prōstĭtūta, ae, f., a harlot, prostitute, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
Trop., unchaste: sermones prostituti ac theatrales,

la:noun:Proserpina.html:
Prō^serpĭna, ae, f., = Περσεφόνη.
Proserpine, daughter of Ceres and Jupiter, and wife of Pluto, who seized her as she was gathering flowers in Sicily, and carried her away to the infernal regions: Cereris Proserpina puer,; cf. ; ; ; .—
Poet., for the Lower World: sed me Imperiosa trahit Proserpina: vive, valeque,.

la:noun:prostitutio.html:
prōstĭtūtĭo, ōnis, f.
prostituo
.
Prostitution, ; ; .—Plur.: mulierum,.—
In gen., a dishonoring, profaning: imaginum,.

la:noun:prostibulum.html:
prōstĭbŭlum, i, n.
id.
.
A prostitute, ; .—
Transf., a male who prostitutes himself, .—
A brothel, ; ; also, in transf. signif., id. Joel, 3, 3.

la:verb:proscindo.gloss: to tear open in front, rend, split, cleave, cut up
senses: to tear open in front, rend, split, cleave, cut up
to plough or break up the land
to censure, castigate, revile, defame, satirize
la:verb:proscindo.html:
prō-scindo, scĭdi, scissum, 3, v. a.,
to tear open in front, to rend, split, cleave, cut up, cut in pieces (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.
In gen.: ferro proscindere quercum,: piscem, and 20: spumanti Rhodanus proscindens gurgite campos,: vulnere pectus,: fulgure terram,.—
In partic., in agriculture, of the first ploughing, to break up the land: rursum terram cum primum arant, proscindere appellant; cum iterum, offringere dicunt, quod primā aratione glebae grandes solent excitari. ; : terram transversis adversisque sulcis,: priusquam ares, proscindito, Cato ap. : bubulcum autem per proscissum ingredi oportet, the trench, furrow, ; ; .—Poet., in gen., for arare, to plough: rorulentas terras, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 496 Rib.): validis terram proscinde juvencis,: terram pressis aratris,: ferro campum,.—
Transf., to cut through, to cleave, furrow (poet.): rostro ventosum aequor. : remo stagna,.—
Trop., to cut up with words, to censure, satirize, revile, defame: aliquem,: equestrem ordinem,: aliquem foedissimo convicio,: carminibus proscissus,: aliquem famoso carmine, Luc.; ; .

la:adj:proselytus.html:
prŏsēlўtus, a, um, = προσήλυτος,
come from abroad, foreign, strange (late Lat.): numeravit Salomon omnes viros proselytos,.—Hence, as subst.,
prŏsēlўtus, i, m.
A sojourner, a stranger in the land: proselyti et advenae,; .—
Esp., one that has come over from heathenism to the Jewish religion, a proselyte (postclass.), ; , n. 8; ; , n. 101.—
prŏsēlўta, ae, f., a female proselyte, converted woman, .

one that has come over from heathenism to the Jewish religion, a proselyte
